+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1592 REGs for the FaAgent ERROR_PATTERNS override (bench/harbor_fa).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+
+Incident (run 38271607849, shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
+gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj): after the 900s timeout ladder kill, harbor's
+failed-command classifier scanned the launch exec's tee'd output with
+``ErrorPattern(r"rate.?limit", ApiRateLimitError)`` — an UNANCHORED
+substring regex. fa's own output legitimately contains the words
+"rate limit" (echoed provider-error text, fa's ``[roles] rate limited
+on … — retrying`` notices), so the failed exec surfaced as
+ApiRateLimitError (``Classified failed command as ApiRateLimitError
+(pattern: 'rate.?limit')``) even though no provider 429 existed.
+
+The fix (gh-1592) is the FaAgent ERROR_PATTERNS override in fa_agent.py:
+the inherited harbor table minus the two unanchored ApiRateLimitError
+entries, replaced with line-anchored equivalents that require the
+structured provider-error context — ``429`` and the wording on the SAME
+line (fa renders real provider errors as ``429: <message>``,
+``HTTP/1.1 429 …``, or single-line JSON ``"code": 429 …``).
+
+Two suites live here:
+
+- AnchoredPatternSemanticsTest — stdlib-only: pins the anchored
+  patterns' semantics against teardown-style and real-429 outputs by
+  compiling FaAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS the way harbor does. Runs with or
+  without the real harbor package.
+- RealClassifierRegressionTest — needs the real harbor 0.23.0 (as
+  installed by bench-harbor.yml before `unittest discover`): drives the
+  REAL ``_classify_exec_error`` end to end.
+"""
+import importlib
+import importlib.util
+import dataclasses
+import re
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_REPO_BENCH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+_REPO_ROOT = _REPO_BENCH.parent
+
+# The harbor stub some sibling test modules install poisons sys.modules;
+# gh-1592 needs the REAL error-pattern surface when the package is
+# available (bench-harbor.yml installs harbor[modal]==0.23.0 before the
+# discover step). Evict and re-import so this module always sees either
+# the real classes or nothing.
+for _name in [
+    n for n in sys.modules if n == "harbor" or n.startswith("harbor.")
+]:
+    del sys.modules[_name]
+try:
+    harbor_base = importlib.import_module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
+    REAL_HARBOR_BASE = harbor_base
+except ImportError:
+    REAL_HARBOR_BASE = None
+
+# The anchored-only stdlib suite still needs fa_agent importable when the
+# real harbor is absent: reuse the sibling module's minimal harbor stub
+# surface (same shape test_fa_agent.py installs), without importing that
+# module — unittest discovery orders modules alphabetically and this file
+# may load first.
+if REAL_HARBOR_BASE is None:
+    def _module(name):
+        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(
+            importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec(name, None)
+        )
+        mod.__fa_harbor_stub__ = True
+        sys.modules[name] = mod
+        return mod
+
+    harbor = _module("harbor")
+    harbor.__path__ = []
+    agents = _module("harbor.agents")
+    harbor.agents = agents
+    agents.__path__ = []
+    installed = _module("harbor.agents.installed")
+    agents.installed = installed
+    installed.__path__ = []
+    installed_base = _module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
+    agents.installed.base = installed_base
+
+    class _StubBaseInstalledAgent:
+        ERROR_PATTERNS = []
+
+    @dataclasses.dataclass
+    class _StubErrorPattern:
+        pattern: str
+        exception: type
+
+    installed_base.BaseInstalledAgent = _StubBaseInstalledAgent
+    installed_base.ErrorPattern = _StubErrorPattern
+    installed_base.ApiRateLimitError = type(
+        "ApiRateLimitError", (RuntimeError,), {}
+    )
+
+    def _load_fa_agent():
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+            "fa_agent_gh1592", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fa_agent.py"
+        )
+        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        sys.modules["fa_agent_gh1592"] = module
+        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        return module
+
+    fa_agent = _load_fa_agent()
+else:
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+        "fa_agent_gh1592", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fa_agent.py"
+    )
+    fa_agent = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules["fa_agent_gh1592"] = fa_agent
+    spec.loader.exec_module(fa_agent)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Fixtures. No stray standalone "429" tokens outside the intended provider
+# error lines — the anchor is \b429\b on the same line.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# The incident shape: a timeout-killed launch exec whose tee'd output
+# mentions rate limits in unrelated contexts (fa's own roles notice, an
+# echoed provider 502 body quoting rate-limit guidance, a teardown grep).
+TEARDOWN_OUTPUT = "\n".join([
+    "[roles] rate limited on z_ai/glm-4.7 — retrying in 5.0s (attempt 2)",
+    "the upstream 502 body echoed: Rate Limit guidance for org-ab12 "
+    "(upstream outage, not throttling)",
+    "teardown poll: grep -i \"rate limit\" /logs/agent/fa.txt || true",
+    "Ratelimits doc referenced in task prose: see docs/rate-limiting.md",
+    "__FA_EXIT=143",
+])
+
+# Free-text rate-limit wordings WITHOUT a 429 on their line must not
+# classify — including when a real 429 exists on a DIFFERENT line (the
+# same-line rule is deliberately line-scoped; gh-1592 fix note).
+STATUSLESS_RATE_LIMIT_OUTPUTS = [
+    TEARDOWN_OUTPUT,
+    # 429 and the wording split across lines: no same-line context.
+    "Error: 429 request rejected by gateway\n"
+    "upstream said: rate limit exhausted for this org",
+    "[roles] too many requests observed on dial/dial-model — backing off",
+    "Provider chain exhausted: every chain model is rate limited and "
+    "cooling down.",
+]
+
+# Real provider-error signatures: 429 and the wording share ONE line.
+REAL_429_OUTPUTS = [
+    # fa's formatProviderError shape (lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart):
+    # '<statusCode>: <message>'.
+    "Error: 429: Rate limit reached for gpt-x on tokens per min ( TPM )",
+    # Raw HTTP status line.
+    "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests",
+    # Single-line JSON body with the structured error code.
+    '{"error":{"message":"Rate limit reached","code":429}}',
+    # Anthropic envelope wording, status prefix on the same line.
+    "429: {\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_error\"}}",
+    # Wording first, status later on the same provider line.
+    "rate limit exceeded — status 429, retry after 5s",
+    # Case-insensitive over the whole match, buried mid-output.
+    "step 1 ok\nREQUEST FAILED: 429 RATE LIMIT EXCEEDED\nstep 2 never ran",
+]
+
+
+def _rate_limit_patterns():
+    """FaAgent's ApiRateLimitError patterns, compiled as harbor does."""
+    return [
+        (re.compile(p.pattern, re.IGNORECASE), p.exception)
+        for p in fa_agent.FaAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
+        if p.exception.__name__ == "ApiRateLimitError"
+    ]
+
+
+def _any_rate_limit_match(text):
+    return any(
+        compiled.search(text) is not None for compiled, _ in _rate_limit_patterns()
+    )
+
+
+class AnchoredPatternSemanticsTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Stdlib-only: the anchored ApiRateLimitError patterns' semantics."""
+
+    def test_override_replaces_unanchored_rate_limit_patterns(self):
+        # The override must exist and keep exactly the anchored
+        # ApiRateLimitError entries — the inherited broad pair is gone
+        # (replaced one-for-one, neither dropped nor grown).
+        ApiRateLimitError = _api_rate_limit_error_cls()
+        inherited = [
+            p
+            for p in _inherited_error_patterns()
+            if p.exception is ApiRateLimitError
+        ]
+        overridden = [c.pattern for c, _ in _rate_limit_patterns()]
+        self.assertEqual(len(overridden), len(inherited))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            len(overridden),
+            2,
+            f"expected exactly the two rate-limit wordings anchored; got "
+            f"{overridden}",
+        )
+        for unanchored in (p.pattern for p in inherited):
+            self.assertNotIn(
+                unanchored,
+                overridden,
+                f"unanchored pattern {unanchored!r} survived the override",
+            )
+
+    def test_teardown_output_with_rate_limit_words_is_not_rate_limit(self):
+        # THE gh-1592 REG: teardown/echo text containing "rate limit"
+        # (and the toomany-requests sibling wording) must not match any
+        # ApiRateLimitError pattern. Pre-fix the broad `rate.?limit`
+        # substring regex matches TEARDOWN_OUTPUT.
+        for text in STATUSLESS_RATE_LIMIT_OUTPUTS:
+            with self.subTest(text=text[:60]):
+                self.assertFalse(_any_rate_limit_match(text))
+
+    def test_real_429_signatures_still_classify(self):
+        # Recall guard: every structured provider-error signature keeps
+        # classifying — 429 and the wording on the SAME line.
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(_rate_limit_patterns()), 1)
+        for text in REAL_429_OUTPUTS:
+            with self.subTest(text=text[:60]):
+                self.assertTrue(_any_rate_limit_match(text))
+
+    def test_non_rate_limit_table_entries_survive_the_override(self):
+        # The override filters ONLY the ApiRateLimitError family: every
+        # other inherited exception keeps its entries.
+        ApiRateLimitError = _api_rate_limit_error_cls()
+        inherited_others = [
+            p for p in _inherited_error_patterns()
+            if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
+        ]
+        overridden_others = [
+            p for p in fa_agent.FaAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
+            if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [(p.pattern, p.exception) for p in inherited_others],
+            [(p.pattern, p.exception) for p in overridden_others],
+        )
+
+
+def _api_rate_limit_error_cls():
+    if REAL_HARBOR_BASE is not None:
+        return REAL_HARBOR_BASE.ApiRateLimitError
+    return sys.modules["harbor.agents.installed.base"].ApiRateLimitError
+
+
+def _inherited_error_patterns():
+    if REAL_HARBOR_BASE is not None:
+        return REAL_HARBOR_BASE.BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
+    return sys.modules[
+        "harbor.agents.installed.base"
+    ].BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    REAL_HARBOR_BASE is not None,
+    "real harbor package not installed (pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0')"
+)
+class RealClassifierRegressionTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Drives harbor's REAL _classify_exec_error end to end (gh-1592)."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.agent = fa_agent.FaAgent(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "logs")
+
+    def _classify(self, stdout):
+        result = type("ExecResult", (), {})()
+        result.return_code = 143
+        result.stdout = stdout
+        result.stderr = ""
+        command = (
+            "set -o pipefail; fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions "
+            "-p 'instruction' < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee /logs/agent/fa.txt"
+        )
+        return self.agent._classify_exec_error(command, result)
+
+    def test_timeout_killed_teardown_output_is_not_api_rate_limit(self):
+        # THE incident: after the 900s ladder kill the launch exec fails
+        # and its tee'd output mentions rate limits — the classification
+        # must be the generic non-zero-exit error, never
+        # ApiRateLimitError (which harbor's retry policy retries on).
+        NonZeroAgentExitCodeError = REAL_HARBOR_BASE.NonZeroAgentExitCodeError
+        error = self._classify(TEARDOWN_OUTPUT)
+        self.assertNotIsInstance(error, REAL_HARBOR_BASE.ApiRateLimitError)
+        self.assertIsInstance(error, NonZeroAgentExitCodeError)
+
+    def test_statusless_rate_limit_prose_is_not_api_rate_limit(self):
+        for text in STATUSLESS_RATE_LIMIT_OUTPUTS:
+            with self.subTest(text=text[:60]):
+                error = self._classify(text)
+                self.assertNotIsInstance(
+                    error, REAL_HARBOR_BASE.ApiRateLimitError
+                )
+
+    def test_real_429_output_still_classifies_api_rate_limit(self):
+        for text in REAL_429_OUTPUTS:
+            with self.subTest(text=text[:60]):
+                error = self._classify(text)
+                self.assertIsInstance(error, REAL_HARBOR_BASE.ApiRateLimitError)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1593
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1593
- **Title**: gh-1592 [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1592` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +374
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T18:32:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:39:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1592
### Root Cause

- harbor 0.23.0's failed-command classifier (`BaseInstalledAgent._classify_exec_error`) scans a failed exec's full stdout+stderr with `ERROR_PATTERNS`, and its `ApiRateLimitError` entries are **unanchored substrings** — `rate.?limit` matches the words "rate limit" anywhere in output.
- fa's tee'd output legitimately contains those words (echoed provider-error text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so after the 900s timeout kill (run 38271607849) the failed launch exec was tagged `ApiRateLimitError` with no provider 429 anywhere. - New `bench/harbor_fa/test_error_classifier.py` — 7 REGs: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must not classify as `ApiRateLimitError` (drove harbor's real `_classify_exec_error`, 10 failures pre-fix); statusless prose and cross-line 429s stay unclassified; real 429 signatures still classify (recall guard); the override keeps all non-rate-limit entries.

### Notes

- Recall tradeoff (accepted, ticket-prescribed): a real 429 whose status and wording land on *different* lines no longer classifies as `ApiRateLimitError` (fa renders provider errors as `<statusCode>: <message>`, so this is not the observed shape). Pattern anchored with `(?im)` inline flags — CI runs Python 3.13, where inline flags must lead the pattern.
- Upstream harbor still ships the broad patterns; the override is pinned to the adapter's 0.23.0 contract.

# gh-1592: [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError

## Description

- **Severity:** minor (no wrong outcomes observed — trial error class stayed AgentTimeoutError; classifier feeds logs/telemetry only)

## Where
`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` — the failed-command classifier that tags exceptions for retry decisions/reporting.

## Incident
Run 38271607849, shard `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5`, trial `gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj` (`job.log`, after the 900s timeout kill):

```
Command failed
Classified failed command as ApiRateLimitError (pattern: 'rate.?limit')
Exception AgentTimeoutError is in exclude_exceptions, not retrying
```

The teardown/poll command output contained the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error text), so the substring regex `rate.?limit` tagged it `ApiRateLimitError` — it was not a 429.

## Fix
- Anchor the classifier: match structured provider-error signatures (HTTP status / JSON `error.code`), not free-text substrings; at minimum require an explicit status context (`429`/`rate limit` in the SAME provider error line, not anywhere in command output).
- Add a regression test: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must NOT classify as ApiRateLimitError.
- Audit sibling patterns in the same classifier table for the same free-text-substring class of bug.

## Related
#1588 (fa-side retry classification — different layer, same theme: error classes must be structural, not vibes).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent):
    # gh-1592: the inherited table's rate-limit entries are free-text
    # substrings (see _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS above) — replace the
    # pair, keep every other entry (auth, usage-limit, capacity, safety,
    # transport, the `API Error` catch-all) byte-identical so the rest of
    # harbor's classification policy is untouched. Matching is
    # position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries
    # also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying
    # both.
    ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        p
        for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
        if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
    ] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS

    @staticmethod
    def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])
        # gh-1556 AC7: fa's deadline awareness rides the same env — the
        # adapter's effective kill cap minus the wrap-up margin, computed
        # once when the deadline run starts (see _run_with_deadline, which
        # stashes the exact value the audit then records). With no timeout
        # knob there is no adapter cap (the dataset-declared task caps are
        # harbor's own) and the export is absent: fa never invents a clock.
        deadline = getattr(self, "_deadline_epoch_ms", None)
        if deadline is not None:
            env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"] = str(deadline)
        return env

    async def install(self, environment: BaseEnvironment) -> None:
        tarball = self._bundle_tarball
        if not tarball.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"fa bundle tarball not found: {tarball} — build it with "
                f"`dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart`"
            )
        remote_tarball = "/tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        await environment.upload_file(tarball, remote_tarball)
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                f"mkdir -p /opt/fa && tar -xzf {remote_tarball} -C /opt/fa && "
                "chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah && ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa"
            ),
        )
        # Task images ship without CA roots — Dart TLS then dies with
        # CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on the provider handshake (live smoke,
        # run 34741686224). Best-effort bootstrap across common distros;
        # a no-op where the store already exists.
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                "if [ ! -e /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then "
                "if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then "
                "apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq ca-certificates; "
                "elif command -v apk >/dev/null; then apk add --no-cache ca-certificates; "
                "elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then dnf install -y ca-certificates; "
                "elif command -v yum >/dev/null; then yum install -y ca-certificates; "
                "fi; fi || true"
            ),
        )
        # No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
        # critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
        await self.exec_as_agent(
            environment,
            command=(
                "mkdir -p ~/.fah && "
                "grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null || "
                "printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml"
            ),
        )
        await self.exec_as_agent(environment, command="fa --version")

    async def run(
        self,
        instruction: str,
        environment: BaseEnvironment,
        context: AgentContext,
    ) -> None:
        knobs = _timeout.TimeoutKnobs.from_env()
        if knobs is None:
            # gh-1556 AC7: no adapter cap => no deadline export (also
            # clear any stash from a previous supervised run on a
            # re-used agent object — fa never sees a stale clock).
            self._deadline_epoch_ms = None
            await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
            return
        await self._run_with_deadline(knobs, instruction, environment)

    def _agent_command(self, instruction: str) -> str:
        # shlex-quote the instruction: backticks/$()/markdown spans in task
        # descriptions must reach fa verbatim (same reason cline quotes).
        return (
            "set -o pipefail; "
            f"mkdir -p {_SESSION_ROOT} && "
            f"fa --session-root {_SESSION_ROOT} "
            f"-p {shlex.quote(instruction)} < /dev/null 2>&1 | "
            "tee /logs/agent/fa.txt; "
            "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}; "
            'echo "__FA_EXIT=${status}" | tee -a /logs/agent/fa.txt; '
            'exit "${status}"'
        )

    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.
        """
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG).
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(knobs)
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(knobs)
        )
        # gh-1556 AC7: the wrap-up deadline exported to fa (via
        # _provider_env) is computed once here, at run start, and the
        # audit below records this exact value.
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = _timeout.deadline_epoch_ms(
            knobs, int(time.time() * 1000)
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        while not exec_task.done():
            remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
            await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
            outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
            )
            if outcome:
                # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                # bounds the trial.
                try:
                    await self.exec_as_root(
                        environment,
                        command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                        timeout_sec=15,
                    )
                except Exception:
                    pass
                try:
                    await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                except Exception:
                    pass
                if not exec_task.done():
                    exec_task.cancel()
                    # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                    # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                    # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                    # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                    # this coroutine still propagates.
                    try:
                        await exec_task
                    except asyncio.CancelledError:
                        if not exec_task.cancelled():
                            raise
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                break
        # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
        # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
        # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
        # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
        error = None
        if not outcome:
            try:
                await exec_task
            except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                error = exc
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, knobs, ladder,
            outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
        )
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

    async def _progress_bytes(self, environment) -> int | None:
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command="wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null",
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and result.stdout:
                return int(result.stdout.strip() or 0)
        except Exception:
            pass
        return None

    async def _write_audit(
        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None
    ) -> None:
        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.
        # AC6 (issue #1185): the audit also documents the harness-originated
        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken
        # where the file lives (one exec, no stream round-trip: a 600s+
        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
        # would make len(utf-8) disagree with the ladder's live wc -c).
        # Fields drop when the stream is unreadable, never fabricated.
        progress, liveness = await self._measure_streams(environment)
        payload = base64.b64encode(
            json.dumps(
                _timeout.audit_dict(
                    knobs,
                    ladder,
                    outcome,
                    progress_bytes=progress,
                    liveness_bytes=liveness,
                    deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_epoch_ms,
                )
            ).encode()
        ).decode()
        try:
            await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    f"mkdir -p /logs/agent && printf %s {payload} "
                    f"| base64 -d > {_AUDIT_PATH}"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    async def _measure_streams(self, environment) -> tuple[int | None, int | None]:
        """Byte-exact (progress, liveness) for the AC6 audit.

        progress = `wc -c` on the pane stream — the same measure the
        ladder's `_progress_bytes` samples, so both auditors agree.
        liveness = byte count of fa's liveness lines inside it — BOTH
        families, matching [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of]: the ⏳
        tool-liveness lines (gh-1055) and the `… reasoning`
        reasoning-liveness lines (gh-1198/gh-1430). grep passes whole
        lines through, `wc -c` counts them; grep terminates a final
        unterminated line, the only ±1 w.r.t. the pure-Python rule in
        [_timeout.liveness_bytes_of] — an audit heuristic, not a spec).
        """
        try:
            result = await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    "if p=$(wc -c < /logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null); then "
                    "l=$(grep -hF -e '\u23f3' -e '… reasoning' "
                    "/logs/agent/fa.txt 2>/dev/null "
                    "| wc -c); "
                    "printf '%s %s' \"$p\" \"$l\"; fi"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
            if result.return_code == 0 and (result.stdout or "").strip():
                progress, _, liveness = result.stdout.strip().partition(" ")
                if progress:
                    return (int(progress), int(liveness or 0))
        except Exception:
            pass
        return (None, None)

    def populate_context_post_run(self, context: AgentContext) -> None:
        """Fold fa's session token accounting into the agent context (issue #1123).

        fa session JSONL assistant records embed
        ``message.usage = {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, ...}``
        (Usage.toJson in lib/src/types.dart); summed across records this is
        the billed usage for the trial. Extraction is shared with the legacy
        adapter (bench/fa_usage.py): rglob covers retries and subagent
        sessions (E1/E2), records with omitted usage contribute a chars/4
        estimate tallied in context.metadata, and a missing/corrupt log
        leaves zeros + a warning.

        Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens INCLUDES cache tokens. cost_usd
        comes from the pinned bench price table (bench/pricing.json);
        unpriced model → None, which the summary renders as n/a.
        """
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(self.logs_dir / "fah-sessions")
        for warning in usage.warnings:
            print(f"[fa_agent] warning: {warning}", file=sys.stderr)
        if not (
            usage.input_tokens
            or usage.output_tokens
            or usage.cache_read_tokens
            or usage.cache_write_tokens
            or usage.estimated_tokens
        ):
            return
        context.n_input_tokens = (
            context.n_input_tokens or 0
        ) + usage.input_tokens + usage.cache_read_tokens + (
            usage.cache_write_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens
        )
        context.n_output_tokens = (
            context.n_output_tokens or 0
        ) + usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens
        context.n_cache_tokens = (
            context.n_cache_tokens or 0
        ) + usage.cache_read_tokens + usage.cache_write_tokens
        pricing = fa_usage.load_pricing(_PRICING_PATH)
        total = 0.0
        priced = bool(usage.models)
        for model, tally in sorted(usage.models.items()):
            cost = fa_usage.cost_usd(
                fa_usage.price_entry(pricing, model),
                tally["input"],
                tally["output"],
                tally["cacheRead"],
                tally["cacheWrite"],
            )
            if cost is None:
                # E3: a model the table doesn't pin → no made-up total.
                priced = False
                print(
                    f"[fa_agent] warning: no bench price for model '{model or '?'}'; "
                    f"cost_usd stays n/a",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
            else:
                total += cost
        context.cost_usd = total if priced else None
        if usage.estimated_tokens:
            context.metadata = {
                **(context.metadata or {}),
                "estimated_tokens": usage.estimated_tokens,
            }


def _b64(value: str) -> str:
    return base64.b64encode(value.encode()).decode()

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1593
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1593
- **Title**: gh-1592 [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1592` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +374
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T18:32:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:39:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1592
### Root Cause

- harbor 0.23.0's failed-command classifier (`BaseInstalledAgent._classify_exec_error`) scans a failed exec's full stdout+stderr with `ERROR_PATTERNS`, and its `ApiRateLimitError` entries are **unanchored substrings** — `rate.?limit` matches the words "rate limit" anywhere in output.
- fa's tee'd output legitimately contains those words (echoed provider-error text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so after the 900s timeout kill (run 38271607849) the failed launch exec was tagged `ApiRateLimitError` with no provider 429 anywhere. Trial verdict stayed `AgentTimeoutError` (severity minor), but a fa run exiting non-zero naturally while mentioning rate limits would be retried under the wrong class.

### Fix

- `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`: `FaAgent` now overrides the `ERROR_PATTERNS` ClassVar — inherited harbor table minus the two unanchored `ApiRateLimitError` entries (`rate.?limit`, `too many requests`), replaced with line-anchored equivalents requiring `429` and the wording on the **same line** (real 429s reach fa output as `429: <message>`, `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, or single-line JSON `"code": 429`; `^` anchoring keeps classification linear over multi-MB streams). Every other entry (usage-limit, auth, capacity, safety, transport, `API Error` catch-all) is byte-identical.
- Sibling-pattern audit (in `outputs/rca.md`): `too many requests` anchored; usage-limit/safety entries are full-sentence signatures; the transport family shares the substring class but has no status code to anchor on — left as-is, noted for upstream.

### Test Coverage

- New `bench/harbor_fa/test_error_classifier.py` — 7 REGs: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must not classify as `ApiRateLimitError` (drove harbor's real `_classify_exec_error`, 10 failures pre-fix); statusless prose and cross-line 429s stay unclassified; real 429 signatures still classify (recall guard); the override keeps all non-rate-limit entries.
- `python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` → 88 tests OK; `-s bench/terminal_bench` → 357 tests OK (harbor 0.23.0 + terminal-bench 0.2.18 installed, same as the bench-harbor.yml gate). No Dart files touched.

### Notes

- Recall tradeoff (accepted, ticket-prescribed): a real 429 whose status and wording land on *different* lines no longer classifies as `ApiRateLimitError` (fa renders provider errors as `<statusCode>: <message>`, so this is not the observed shape). Pattern anchored with `(?im)` inline flags — CI runs Python 3.13, where inline flags must lead the pattern.
- Upstream harbor still ships the broad patterns; the override is pinned to the adapter's 0.23.0 contract.

# gh-1592: [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError

## Description

- **Severity:** minor (no wrong outcomes observed — trial error class stayed AgentTimeoutError; classifier feeds logs/telemetry only)

## Where
`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` — the failed-command classifier that tags exceptions for retry decisions/reporting.

## Incident
Run 38271607849, shard `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5`, trial `gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj` (`job.log`, after the 900s timeout kill):

```
Command failed
Classified failed command as ApiRateLimitError (pattern: 'rate.?limit')
Exception AgentTimeoutError is in exclude_exceptions, not retrying
```

The teardown/poll command output contained the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error text), so the substring regex `rate.?limit` tagged it `ApiRateLimitError` — it was not a 429.

## Fix
- Anchor the classifier: match structured provider-error signatures (HTTP status / JSON `error.code`), not free-text substrings; at minimum require an explicit status context (`429`/`rate limit` in the SAME provider error line, not anywhere in command output).
- Add a regression test: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must NOT classify as ApiRateLimitError.
- Audit sibling patterns in the same classifier table for the same free-text-substring class of bug.

## Related
#1588 (fa-side retry classification — different layer, same theme: error classes must be structural, not vibes).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent):
    # gh-1592: the inherited table's rate-limit entries are free-text
    # substrings (see _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS above) — replace the
    # pair, keep every other entry (auth, usage-limit, capacity, safety,
    # transport, the `API Error` catch-all) byte-identical so the rest of
    # harbor's classification policy is untouched. Matching is
    # position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries
    # also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying
    # both.
    ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        p
        for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
        if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
    ] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS

    @staticmethod
    def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1593
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1593
- **Title**: gh-1592 [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1592` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +374
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T18:32:57Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:39:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #1592
### Root Cause

- harbor 0.23.0's failed-command classifier (`BaseInstalledAgent._classify_exec_error`) scans a failed exec's full stdout+stderr with `ERROR_PATTERNS`, and its `ApiRateLimitError` entries are **unanchored substrings** — `rate.?limit` matches the words "rate limit" anywhere in output.
- fa's tee'd output legitimately contains those words (echoed provider-error text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so after the 900s timeout kill (run 38271607849) the failed launch exec was tagged `ApiRateLimitError` with no provider 429 anywhere. Trial verdict stayed `AgentTimeoutError` (severity minor), but a fa run exiting non-zero naturally while mentioning rate limits would be retried under the wrong class.

### Fix

- `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`: `FaAgent` now overrides the `ERROR_PATTERNS` ClassVar — inherited harbor table minus the two unanchored `ApiRateLimitError` entries (`rate.?limit`, `too many requests`), replaced with line-anchored equivalents requiring `429` and the wording on the **same line** (real 429s reach fa output as `429: <message>`, `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, or single-line JSON `"code": 429`; `^` anchoring keeps classification linear over multi-MB streams). Every other entry (usage-limit, auth, capacity, safety, transport, `API Error` catch-all) is byte-identical.
- Sibling-pattern audit (in `outputs/rca.md`): `too many requests` anchored; usage-limit/safety entries are full-sentence signatures; the transport family shares the substring class but has no status code to anchor on — left as-is, noted for upstream.

### Test Coverage

- New `bench/harbor_fa/test_error_classifier.py` — 7 REGs: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must not classify as `ApiRateLimitError` (drove harbor's real `_classify_exec_error`, 10 failures pre-fix); statusless prose and cross-line 429s stay unclassified; real 429 signatures still classify (recall guard); the override keeps all non-rate-limit entries.
- `python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` → 88 tests OK; `-s bench/terminal_bench` → 357 tests OK (harbor 0.23.0 + terminal-bench 0.2.18 installed, same as the bench-harbor.yml gate). No Dart files touched.

### Notes

- Recall tradeoff (accepted, ticket-prescribed): a real 429 whose status and wording land on *different* lines no longer classifies as `ApiRateLimitError` (fa renders provider errors as `<statusCode>: <message>`, so this is not the observed shape). Pattern anchored with `(?im)` inline flags — CI runs Python 3.13, where inline flags must lead the pattern.
- Upstream harbor still ships the broad patterns; the override is pinned to the adapter's 0.23.0 contract.

# gh-1592: [BUG] bench adapter error classifier: regex 'rate.?limit' misclassifies timeout-teardown failures as ApiRateLimitError

## Description

- **Severity:** minor (no wrong outcomes observed — trial error class stayed AgentTimeoutError; classifier feeds logs/telemetry only)

## Where
`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py` — the failed-command classifier that tags exceptions for retry decisions/reporting.

## Incident
Run 38271607849, shard `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5`, trial `gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj` (`job.log`, after the 900s timeout kill):

```
Command failed
Classified failed command as ApiRateLimitError (pattern: 'rate.?limit')
Exception AgentTimeoutError is in exclude_exceptions, not retrying
```

The teardown/poll command output contained the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error text), so the substring regex `rate.?limit` tagged it `ApiRateLimitError` — it was not a 429.

## Fix
- Anchor the classifier: match structured provider-error signatures (HTTP status / JSON `error.code`), not free-text substrings; at minimum require an explicit status context (`429`/`rate limit` in the SAME provider error line, not anywhere in command output).
- Add a regression test: teardown output containing "rate limit" inside unrelated text must NOT classify as ApiRateLimitError.
- Audit sibling patterns in the same classifier table for the same free-text-substring class of bug.

## Related
#1588 (fa-side retry classification — different layer, same theme: error classes must be structural, not vibes).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
