"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent):
    # gh-1592: the inherited table's rate-limit entries are free-text
    # substrings (see _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS above) — replace the
    # pair, keep every other entry (auth, usage-limit, capacity, safety,
    # transport, the `API Error` catch-all) byte-identical so the rest of
    # harbor's classification policy is untouched. Matching is
    # position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries
    # also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying
    # both.
    ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        p
        for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
        if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
    ] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS

    @staticmethod
    def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }

        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])

class NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the agent process exits with a non-zero exit code."""

    pass


class ApiError(NonZeroAgentExitCodeError):
    """Base class for model provider API errors detected in agent output."""

    pass


class ApiRateLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rate-limited a request.

    The distinct type name lets retry policy target it, e.g.
    ``harbor run --max-retries 3 --retry-include ApiRateLimitError``.
    """

    pass


class ApiUsageLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rejected the request because an account or project usage limit is exhausted.
    """

    pass


class ApiInternalServerError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    returns a 500 Internal Server Error.
    """

    pass


class ApiOverloadedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    is temporarily overloaded or unavailable.
    """

    pass


class ApiConnectionClosedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    closed the connection before the response completed.
    """

    pass


class ApiResponseStalledError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    response stalled mid-stream before completing.
    """

    pass


class OutputTokenExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model response
    exceeded the configured output token maximum.
    """

    pass


class ContextWindowExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the request exceeded
    the model's context window.
    """

    pass


class UnknownApiError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates an unclassified
    model provider API error.
    """

    pass

def _redact_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Mask values of ``Cli(sensitive=True)`` options wherever they appear.

        Sensitive flag values (e.g. auth headers in ``completion_kwargs``) are
        rendered onto the command line, so any log or persisted record of the
        command should scrub them.
        """
        if self.options is None:
            return command
        for secret in sensitive_option_values(self.options):
            if secret:
                [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] = command.replace(secret, "****")
        return command

    def _classify_exec_error(
        self, command: str, result: Any
    ) -> NonZeroAgentExitCodeError:
        """Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS,
        falling back to NonZeroAgentExitCodeError.
        """
        detail = (
            f"Command failed (exit {result.return_code}): "
            f"{self._redact_command(command)}\n"
            f"stdout: {self._truncate_output(result.stdout)}\n"
            f"stderr: {self._truncate_output(result.stderr)}"
        )
        output = f"{result.stdout or ''}\n{result.stderr or ''}"
        # Soft Claude divert continues the run; never ASR from free-text needles
        # alone (explanatory content can mention Usage Policy / filter phrases).
        skip_asr = (
            "model_refusal_fallback" in output
            and "model_refusal_no_fallback" not in output
        )
        last_match: (
            tuple[int, re.Pattern[str], type[NonZeroAgentExitCodeError]] | None
        ) = None
        for compiled, exception in self._compiled_error_patterns:
            if skip_asr and exception is AgentSafetyRefusalError:
                continue
            for match in compiled.finditer(output):
                if last_match is None or match.end() > last_match[0]:
                    last_match = (match.end(), compiled, exception)

        if last_match is not None:
            _, compiled, exception = last_match
            self.logger.debug(
                f"Classified failed command as {exception.__name__} "
                f"(pattern: {compiled.pattern!r})"
            )
            return exception(detail)
        return NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(detail)

1. `ERROR_PATTERNS` is a `ClassVar[list[ErrorPattern]]` on `BaseInstalledAgent`. ✓
2. `ErrorPattern` is a dataclass with `pattern: str` and `exception: type`. Let me verify the ErrorPattern dataclass definition.
3. `_classify_exec_error` compiles with `re.compile(p.pattern, re.IGNORECASE)` — so inline `(?im)` flags work fine in Python (inline flags at the START of the pattern apply globally; since `(?im)` is at the start of the whole pattern string, it's valid in Python 3.11+... wait, actually Python 3.11 deprecated mid-pattern inline flags. `(?im)` at the start is fine in all versions. In Python 3.13, global inline flags not at the start raise errors. The pattern here has `(?im)` at the very start of the string, so it's fine on all versions.

4. `_classify_exec_error` uses position-based matching: "Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS" — iterates all compiled patterns, `finditer` over the output, and keeps the match with the largest `match.end()`. So the classification is by POSITION (last position in output wins), not table order. The PR comment says "Matching is position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Wait — this claim needs scrutiny. The claim: "the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Let's think: if a line matches BOTH the anchored rate-limit pattern AND the generic `API Error` (UnknownApiError) pattern, which wins? Position-based: whichever match ends LATER in the output. 

Consider a real provider error line: `Error: 429: Rate limit reached for gpt-x`. The `API Error` pattern is `r"API Error"` — matches "API Error" ending at column ~9. The rate-limit pattern `(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*rate.?limit[^\r\n]*` matches the whole line starting at line start and ending at line end. So the rate-limit match ends much later → rate limit wins. Good.

But wait — consider a case where the "API Error" catch-all matches on a LATER line than the 429 line. E.g.:
```
Error: 429: Rate limit reached
API Error: something else later
```
The 429 line ends earlier; the "API Error" on a later line ends later → UnknownApiError wins. That's the same behavior as the inherited table (position-based), so no regression there. Actually with the inherited table, `rate.?limit` would match the first line ending at "limit" (~column 26 of line 1), and "API Error" ends later, so UnknownApiError would also win. Same behavior.

But here's a subtle behavioral difference introduced by the anchored patterns: with `^` anchoring and `[^\r\n]*` spans, the anchored pattern's match now spans THE ENTIRE LINE from line start to line end. This extends match.end() to the end of the 429 line. With the old unanchored `rate.?limit`, match ended at "limit" (or "rate limit" end). Hmm, could the extended match end swallow a classification that previously won?

Scenario: a line containing BOTH "429 rate limit" text AND "Connection refused" AFTER it on the same line... e.g. `429 rate limit reached (connection refused?)`. With old pattern: `rate.?limit` ends at ~col 13; `Connection refused` ends at end of line → NetworkConnectionError wins (correct-ish). With new anchored pattern: rate-limit match ends at END of line (because `[^\r\n]*` trailing span) → position tie: both end at line end. `match.end() > last_match[0]` is strict greater-than, so FIRST-compiled wins on ties. Pattern compile order: rate-limit patterns are FIRST in the table (inherited order — after the override, rate-limit entries were originally first; the override filters ApiRateLimitError entries and appends the anchored pair AT THE END). So the anchored rate-limit entries are appended at the END of the table. Compile order: usage-limit, auth, ..., API Error catch-all, network errors, THEN the two anchored rate-limit patterns last.

On a tie (both matches end at the same position), the FIRST pattern in iteration order wins (`match.end() > last_match[0]` strict). So if `Connection refused` on the same line ends at the same position as the anchored rate-limit match (both at line end), the earlier-compiled `Connection refused` pattern wins → NetworkConnectionError. Fine — arguably correct.

Conversely, what if the 429 wording comes AFTER "Connection refused" on the same line, e.g. `Connection refused after 429 rate limit`? Old behavior: `rate.?limit` match ends at "limit" (col ~36); `Connection refused` ends at col ~18 → rate limit wins. New: rate-limit match spans whole line → wins. Same.

Now the more interesting regression class: the trailing `[^\r\n]*` span means the anchored rate-limit match now extends to END of line, so on a same-line tie with any other pattern, the rate-limit pattern (compiled LAST) LOSES the tie (strict >). Example: `429 rate limit — retry (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL detail)` hmm that's contrived.

More important: what about a MULTI-LINE consideration? The pattern is line-scoped (`[^\r\n]*`), so cross-line "429 ... rate limit" doesn't match — that's the accepted recall tradeoff, tested.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent):
    # gh-1592: the inherited table's rate-limit entries are free-text
    # substrings (see _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS above) — replace the
    # pair, keep every other entry (auth, usage-limit, capacity, safety,
    # transport, the `API Error` catch-all) byte-identical so the rest of
    # harbor's classification policy is untouched. Matching is
    # position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries
    # also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying
    # both.
    ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        p
        for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
        if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
    ] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS

    @staticmethod
    def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])

class NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the agent process exits with a non-zero exit code."""

    pass


class ApiError(NonZeroAgentExitCodeError):
    """Base class for model provider API errors detected in agent output."""

    pass


class ApiRateLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rate-limited a request.

    The distinct type name lets retry policy target it, e.g.
    ``harbor run --max-retries 3 --retry-include ApiRateLimitError``.
    """

    pass


class ApiUsageLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rejected the request because an account or project usage limit is exhausted.
    """

    pass


class ApiInternalServerError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    returns a 500 Internal Server Error.
    """

    pass


class ApiOverloadedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    is temporarily overloaded or unavailable.
    """

    pass


class ApiConnectionClosedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    closed the connection before the response completed.
    """

    pass


class ApiResponseStalledError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    response stalled mid-stream before completing.
    """

    pass


class OutputTokenExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model response
    exceeded the configured output token maximum.
    """

    pass


class ContextWindowExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the request exceeded
    the model's context window.
    """

    pass


class UnknownApiError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates an unclassified
    model provider API error.
    """

    pass

def _redact_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Mask values of ``Cli(sensitive=True)`` options wherever they appear.

        Sensitive flag values (e.g. auth headers in ``completion_kwargs``) are
        rendered onto the command line, so any log or persisted record of the
        command should scrub them.
        """
        if self.options is None:
            return command
        for secret in sensitive_option_values(self.options):
            if secret:
                [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] = command.replace(secret, "****")
        return command

    def _classify_exec_error(
        self, command: str, result: Any
    ) -> NonZeroAgentExitCodeError:
        """Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS,
        falling back to NonZeroAgentExitCodeError.
        """
        detail = (
            f"Command failed (exit {result.return_code}): "
            f"{self._redact_command(command)}\n"
            f"stdout: {self._truncate_output(result.stdout)}\n"
            f"stderr: {self._truncate_output(result.stderr)}"

        # Soft Claude divert continues the run; never ASR from free-text needles
        # alone (explanatory content can mention Usage Policy / filter phrases).
        skip_asr = (
            "model_refusal_fallback" in output
            and "model_refusal_no_fallback" not in output
        )
        last_match: (
            tuple[int, re.Pattern[str], type[NonZeroAgentExitCodeError]] | None
        ) = None

                f"Classified failed command as {exception.__name__} "
                f"(pattern: {compiled.pattern!r})"
            )
            return exception(detail)
        return NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(detail)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


class FaAgent(BaseInstalledAgent):
    # gh-1592: the inherited table's rate-limit entries are free-text
    # substrings (see _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS above) — replace the
    # pair, keep every other entry (auth, usage-limit, capacity, safety,
    # transport, the `API Error` catch-all) byte-identical so the rest of
    # harbor's classification policy is untouched. Matching is
    # position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries
    # also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying
    # both.
    ERROR_PATTERNS = [
        p
        for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
        if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
    ] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS

    @staticmethod
    def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])
        # gh-1556 AC7: fa's deadline awareness rides the same env — the

class NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the agent process exits with a non-zero exit code."""

    pass


class ApiError(NonZeroAgentExitCodeError):
    """Base class for model provider API errors detected in agent output."""

    pass


class ApiRateLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rate-limited a request.

    The distinct type name lets retry policy target it, e.g.
    ``harbor run --max-retries 3 --retry-include ApiRateLimitError``.
    """

    pass


class ApiUsageLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rejected the request because an account or project usage limit is exhausted.
    """

    pass


class ApiInternalServerError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    returns a 500 Internal Server Error.
    """

    pass


class ApiOverloadedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    is temporarily overloaded or unavailable.
    """

    pass


class ApiConnectionClosedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    closed the connection before the response completed.
    """

    pass


class ApiResponseStalledError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    response stalled mid-stream before completing.
    """

    pass


class OutputTokenExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model response
    exceeded the configured output token maximum.
    """

    pass


class ContextWindowExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the request exceeded
    the model's context window.
    """

    pass


class UnknownApiError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates an unclassified
    model provider API error.
    """

    pass

def _redact_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Mask values of ``Cli(sensitive=True)`` options wherever they appear.

        Sensitive flag values (e.g. auth headers in ``completion_kwargs``) are
        rendered onto the command line, so any log or persisted record of the
        command should scrub them.
        """
        if self.options is None:
            return command
        for secret in sensitive_option_values(self.options):
            if secret:
                [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] = command.replace(secret, "****")
        return command

    def _classify_exec_error(
        self, command: str, result: Any

        """Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS,
        falling back to NonZeroAgentExitCodeError.

In Python 3.13, global inline flags not at the start raise errors. The pattern here has `(?im)` at the very start of the string, so it's fine on all versions.

So the classification is by POSITION (last position in output wins), not table order. The PR comment says "Matching is position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Let's think: if a line matches BOTH the anchored rate-limit pattern AND the generic `API Error` (UnknownApiError) pattern, which wins? Position-based: whichever match ends LATER in the output. 

Consider a real provider error line: `Error: 429: Rate limit reached for gpt-x`. The `API Error` pattern is `r"API Error"` — matches "API Error" ending at column ~9. The rate-limit pattern `(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*rate.?limit[^\r\n]*` matches the whole line starting at line start and ending at line end. So the rate-limit match ends much later → rate limit wins. Good.

But wait — consider a case where the "API Error" catch-all matches on a LATER line than the 429 line. E.g.:
```

API Error: something else later
```
The 429 line ends earlier; the "API Error" on a later line ends later → UnknownApiError wins. That's the same behavior as the inherited table (position-based), so no regression there. Actually with the inherited table, `rate.?limit` would match the first line ending at "limit" (~column 26 of line 1), and "API Error" ends later, so UnknownApiError would also win. Same behavior.

But here's a subtle behavioral difference introduced by the anchored patterns: with `^` anchoring and `[^\r\n]*` spans, the anchored pattern's match now spans THE ENTIRE LINE from line start to line end. This extends match.end() to the end of the 429 line. With the old unanchored `rate.?limit`, match ended at "limit" (or "rate limit" end). Hmm, could the extended match end swallow a classification that previously won?

Scenario: a line containing BOTH "429 rate limit" text AND "Connection refused" AFTER it on the same line... e.g. `429 rate limit reached (connection refused?)`. With old pattern: `rate.?limit` ends at ~col 13; `Connection refused` ends at end of line → NetworkConnectionError wins (correct-ish). With new anchored pattern: rate-limit match ends at END of line (because `[^\r\n]*` trailing span) → position tie: both end at line end. `match.end() > last_match[0]` is strict greater-than, so FIRST-compiled wins on ties. Now I've verified the harbor internals:

1. `ERROR_PATTERNS` is a `ClassVar[list[ErrorPattern]]` on `BaseInstalledAgent`. ✓
2. `ErrorPattern` is a dataclass with `pattern: str` and `exception: type`. Let me verify the ErrorPattern dataclass definition.
3. `_classify_exec_error` compiles with `re.compile(p.pattern, re.IGNORECASE)` — so inline `(?im)` flags work fine in Python (inline flags at the START of the pattern apply globally; since `(?im)` is at the start of the whole pattern string, it's valid in Python 3.11+... wait, actually Python 3.11 deprecated mid-pattern inline flags. `(?im)` at the start is fine in all versions. In Python 3.13, global inline flags not at the start raise errors. The pattern here has `(?im)` at the very start of the string, so it's fine on all versions.

4. `_classify_exec_error` uses position-based matching: "Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS" — iterates all compiled patterns, `finditer` over the output, and keeps the match with the largest `match.end()`. So the classification is by POSITION (last position in output wins), not table order. The PR comment says "Matching is position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Wait — this claim needs scrutiny. The claim: "the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Let's think: if a line matches BOTH the anchored rate-limit pattern AND the generic `API Error` (UnknownApiError) pattern, which wins? Position-based: whichever match ends LATER in the output. 

Consider a real provider error line: `Error: 429: Rate limit reached for gpt-x`. The `API Error` pattern is `r"API Error"` — matches "API Error" ending at column ~9. The rate-limit pattern `(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*rate.?limit[^\r\n]*` matches the whole line starting at line start and ending at line end. So the rate-limit match ends much later → rate limit wins. Good.

But wait — consider a case where the "API Error" catch-all matches on a LATER line than the 429 line. E.g.:
```
Error: 429: Rate limit reached
API Error: something else later
```
The 429 line ends earlier; the "API Error" on a later line ends later → UnknownApiError wins. That's the same behavior as the inherited table (position-based), so no regression there. Actually with the inherited table, `rate.?limit` would match the first line ending at "limit" (~column 26 of line 1), and "API Error" ends later, so UnknownApiError would also win. Same behavior.

But here's a subtle behavioral difference introduced by the anchored patterns: with `^` anchoring and `[^\r\n]*` spans, the anchored pattern's match now spans THE ENTIRE LINE from line start to line end. This extends match.end() to the end of the 429 line. With the old unanchored `rate.?limit`, match ended at "limit" (or "rate limit" end). Hmm, could the extended match end swallow a classification that previously won?

Scenario: a line containing BOTH "429 rate limit" text AND "Connection refused" AFTER it on the same line... e.g. `429 rate limit reached (connection refused?)`. With old pattern: `rate.?limit` ends at ~col 13; `Connection refused` ends at end of line → NetworkConnectionError wins (correct-ish). With new anchored pattern: rate-limit match ends at END of line (because `[^\r\n]*` trailing span) → position tie: both end at line end. `match.end() > last_match[0]` is strict greater-than, so FIRST-compiled wins on ties. Pattern compile order: rate-limit patterns are FIRST in the table (inherited order — after the override, rate-limit entries were originally first; the override filters ApiRateLimitError entries and appends the anchored pair AT THE END). Wait, let me re-check the override:

```python
ERROR_PATTERNS = [
    p
    for p in BaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS
    if p.exception is not ApiRateLimitError
] + _ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS
```

So the anchored rate-limit entries are appended at the END of the table. Compile order: usage-limit, auth, ..., API Error catch-all, network errors, THEN the two anchored rate-limit patterns last.

On a tie (both matches end at the same position), the FIRST pattern in iteration order wins (`match.end() > last_match[0]` strict). So if `Connection refused` on the same line ends at the same position as the anchored rate-limit match (both at line end), the earlier-compiled `Connection refused` pattern wins → NetworkConnectionError. Fine — arguably correct.

Conversely, what if the 429 wording comes AFTER "Connection refused" on the same line, e.g. `Connection refused after 429 rate limit`? Old behavior: `rate.?limit` match ends at "limit" (col ~36); `Connection refused` ends at col ~18 → rate limit wins. New: rate-limit match spans whole line → wins. Same.

Now the more interesting regression class: the trailing `[^\r\n]*` span means the anchored rate-limit match now extends to END of line, so on a same-line tie with any other pattern, the rate-limit pattern (compiled LAST) LOSES the tie (strict >). Example: `429 rate limit — retry (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL detail)` hmm that's contrived.

More important: what about a MULTI-LINE consideration? The pattern is line-scoped (`[^\r\n]*`), so cross-line "429 ... rate limit" doesn't match — that's the accepted recall tradeoff, tested.

### Thread 1 — `bench/harbor_fa/test_error_classifier.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: harbor-less fallback stub can't load `fa_agent.py` — the "stdlib-only / runs without harbor" claim is false**

The fallback stub here installs only `harbor`, `harbor.agents.*` and `harbor.agents.installed.base`. But `fa_agent.py` also imports `harbor.environments.base.BaseEnvironment` (line 66) and `harbor.models.agent.context.AgentContext` (line 68), so without the real harbor package the module dies at import:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'harbor.environments'
```

Verified on this branch (no harbor installed):

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` → `FAILED (errors=1)` (import error on `test_error_classifier`), while the pre-PR suite passed clean without harbor — sibling modules like `test_fa_agent.py` stub the full surface (`harbor.environments.base`, `harbor.models.agent.context` included).
- With real harbor 0.23.0 installed: 134 tests OK, all module orderings pass — the CI gate (bench-harbor.yml installs harbor first) is unaffected.

Note the comment says the stub is the "same shape test_fa_agent.py installs" — it isn't; `test_fa_agent._install_harbor_stubs()` additionally stubs `harbor.environments(.base)` and `harbor.models(.agent.context)`.

Two pitfalls if you extend the stub:

1. Extending the stub modules alone is **not enough**: `test_override_replaces_unanchored_rate_limit_patterns` asserts `len(overridden) == len(inherited)`; with the stub's empty `ERROR_PATTERNS` that is `2 == 0` and it fails. Seed `_StubBaseInstalledAgent.ERROR_PATTERNS` with at least the two inherited unanchored entries (`ErrorPattern(r"rate.?limit", ApiRateLimitError)`, `ErrorPattern(r"too many requests", ApiRateLimitError)`) so the replacement assertion has something real to bite on.
2. Either shape the fallback like `test_fa_agent.py`'s (share it, or copy the environments/models stubs), or drop the no-harbor path and `skipUnless(REAL_HARBOR_BASE ...)` the whole module so the docstring stops claiming stdlib-only operation.

Minor, same block: `importlib.machinery` is used (`ModuleSpec`) but never imported explicitly — it only resolves transitively via `import importlib.util`.

### Thread 2 — `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `\b429\b` still matches inside decimals — residual FP vector of the same echo-text class**

`429` with word boundaries matches the `429` inside a decimal like `0.429` (`.` is a non-word char, so both sides are boundaries). Verified against real harbor 0.23.0 with the override active:

```
tokens=0.429 rate limit guidance echoed   -> ApiRateLimitError
```

So echoed output that quotes a decimal (`0.429s` backoff, a cost, a probability) on a line that also says "rate limit" re-triggers the misclassification this PR fixes — strictly narrower than the inherited unanchored substring, but not closed. A numeric-context guard closes it:

```python
r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"
```

(keep `\b429\b`'s behavior for `429:`/`HTTP/1.1 429`/`"code": 429` — all still match). Optional given the accepted tradeoff, but it is the one remaining free-text adjacency in the anchor.

### Thread 3 — `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "outrank" mechanism is the full-line span, not table position — and the span reverses one same-line tie-break**

Verified against real harbor 0.23.0 (`_classify_exec_error` keeps the match with the largest `match.end()`; on an exact tie the earlier-compiled pattern wins). The comment is right that the anchored entries beat the `API Error` catch-all on a shared line, but the reason is that the anchored match spans to end-of-line (`[^\r\n]*` tail), not that they're appended last — appended-last actually *loses* exact ties.

The full-line span also flips one edge class vs the pre-fix table (verified):

```
pre-fix:  "429 rate limit exceeded (could not resolve host later)" -> NetworkConnectionError
now:      same line                                                -> ApiRateLimitError
```

The trailing `[^\r\n]*` stretches the rate-limit match past a later same-line network-error needle. Both classes are retryable and the input is contrived (provider 429 lines don't carry DNS/conn phrases), so no action required — but the comment could state the mechanism accurately ("spans to end-of-line, winning the position race") and note the tie-flip, since the next person auditing position semantics will reason from this comment.

class NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the agent process exits with a non-zero exit code."""

    pass


class ApiError(NonZeroAgentExitCodeError):
    """Base class for model provider API errors detected in agent output."""

    pass


class ApiRateLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rate-limited a request.

    The distinct type name lets retry policy target it, e.g.
    ``harbor run --max-retries 3 --retry-include ApiRateLimitError``.
    """

    pass


class ApiUsageLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rejected the request because an account or project usage limit is exhausted.
    """

    pass


class ApiInternalServerError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    returns a 500 Internal Server Error.
    """

    pass


class ApiOverloadedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    is temporarily overloaded or unavailable.
    """

    pass


class ApiConnectionClosedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    closed the connection before the response completed.
    """

    pass


class ApiResponseStalledError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    response stalled mid-stream before completing.
    """

    pass


class OutputTokenExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model response
    exceeded the configured output token maximum.
    """

    pass


class ContextWindowExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the request exceeded
    the model's context window.
    """

    pass


class UnknownApiError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates an unclassified
    model provider API error.
    """

    pass

def _redact_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Mask values of ``Cli(sensitive=True)`` options wherever they appear.

        Sensitive flag values (e.g. auth headers in ``completion_kwargs``) are
        rendered onto the command line, so any log or persisted record of the
        command should scrub them.

        for secret in sensitive_option_values(self.options):
            if secret:

import re

_REPO_BENCH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# The harbor stub some sibling test modules install poisons sys.modules;
# gh-1592 needs the REAL error-pattern surface when the package is
# available (bench-harbor.yml installs harbor[modal]==0.23.0 before the
# discover step). Evict and re-import so this module always sees either
# the real classes or nothing.
for _name in [
    n for n in sys.modules if n == "harbor" or n.startswith("harbor.")
]:
    del sys.modules[_name]
try:
    harbor_base = importlib.import_module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
    REAL_HARBOR_BASE = harbor_base
except ImportError:
    REAL_HARBOR_BASE = None

# The anchored-only stdlib suite still needs fa_agent importable when the
# real harbor is absent: reuse the sibling module's minimal harbor stub
# surface (same shape test_fa_agent.py installs), without importing that
# module — unittest discovery orders modules alphabetically and this file
# may load first.
if REAL_HARBOR_BASE is None:
    def _module(name):
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(
            importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec(name, None)
        )
        mod.__fa_harbor_stub__ = True
        sys.modules[name] = mod
        return mod

    harbor = _module("harbor")
    harbor.__path__ = []
    agents = _module("harbor.agents")
    harbor.agents = agents
    agents.__path__ = []
    installed = _module("harbor.agents.installed")
    agents.installed = installed
    installed.__path__ = []
    installed_base = _module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
    agents.installed.base = installed_base

    class _StubBaseInstalledAgent:
        ERROR_PATTERNS = []

    @dataclasses.dataclass
    class _StubErrorPattern:
        pattern: str
        exception: type

    installed_base.BaseInstalledAgent = _StubBaseInstalledAgent
    installed_base.ErrorPattern = _StubErrorPattern
    installed_base.ApiRateLimitError = type(
        "ApiRateLimitError", (RuntimeError,), {}
    )

    def _load_fa_agent():
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "fa_agent_gh1592", Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fa_agent.py"
        )
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules["fa_agent_gh1592"] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        return module

class NonZeroAgentExitCodeError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the agent process exits with a non-zero exit code."""

    pass


class ApiError(NonZeroAgentExitCodeError):
    """Base class for model provider API errors detected in agent output."""

    pass


class ApiRateLimitError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rate-limited a request.

    The distinct type name lets retry policy target it, e.g.
    ``harbor run --max-retries 3 --retry-include ApiRateLimitError``.

    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    rejected the request because an account or project usage limit is exhausted.

    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    returns a 500 Internal Server Error.

    pass


class ApiOverloadedError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    is temporarily overloaded or unavailable.
    """

    pass

    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider
    closed the connection before the response completed.
    """

    pass

    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model provider

    """

    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the model response

    pass


class ContextWindowExceededError(ApiError):
    """Raised when a failed command's output indicates the request exceeded

    pass

def _redact_command(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Mask values of ``Cli(sensitive=True)`` options wherever they appear.

        Sensitive flag values (e.g. auth headers in ``completion_kwargs``) are
        rendered onto the command line, so any log or persisted record of the
        command should scrub them.

        if self.options is None:

        for secret in sensitive_option_values(self.options):
            if secret:

        return command

    def _classify_exec_error(
        self, command: str, result: Any
    ) -> NonZeroAgentExitCodeError:
        """Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS,
        falling back to NonZeroAgentExitCodeError.
        """
        detail = (
            f"Command failed (exit {result.return_code}): "
            f"{self._redact_command(command)}\n"
            f"stdout: {self._truncate_output(result.stdout)}\n"
            f"stderr: {self._truncate_output(result.stderr)}"

            "model_refusal_fallback" in output

        last_match: (
            tuple[int, re.Pattern[str], type[NonZeroAgentExitCodeError]] | None

1. `ERROR_PATTERNS` is a `ClassVar[list[ErrorPattern]]` on `BaseInstalledAgent`. ✓

3. `_classify_exec_error` compiles with `re.compile(p.pattern, re.IGNORECASE)` — so inline `(?im)` flags work fine in Python (inline flags at the START of the pattern apply globally; since `(?im)` is at the start of the whole pattern string, it's valid in Python 3.11+... wait, actually Python 3.11 deprecated mid-pattern inline flags. `(?im)` at the start is fine in all versions. In Python 3.13, global inline flags not at the start raise errors. The pattern here has `(?im)` at the very start of the string, so it's fine on all versions.

4. `_classify_exec_error` uses position-based matching: "Map a failed command to the last matching error in ERROR_PATTERNS" — iterates all compiled patterns, `finditer` over the output, and keeps the match with the largest `match.end()`. So the classification is by POSITION (last position in output wins), not table order. The PR comment says "Matching is position-based (last match wins), so the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Wait — this claim needs scrutiny. The claim: "the appended anchored entries also outrank the generic `API Error` catch-all on a line carrying both."

Let's think: if a line matches BOTH the anchored rate-limit pattern AND the generic `API Error` (UnknownApiError) pattern, which wins? Position-based: whichever match ends LATER in the output. 

Consider a real provider error line: `Error: 429: Rate limit reached for gpt-x`. The `API Error` pattern is `r"API Error"` — matches "API Error" ending at column ~9. The rate-limit pattern `(?im)^[^\r\n]*\b429\b[^\r\n]*rate.?limit[^\r\n]*` matches the whole line starting at line start and ending at line end. So the rate-limit match ends much later → rate limit wins. Good.

But wait — consider a case where the "API Error" catch-all matches on a LATER line than the 429 line. E.g.:
```
Error: 429: Rate limit reached
API Error: something else later
```
The 429 line ends earlier; the "API Error" on a later line ends later → UnknownApiError wins. That's the same behavior as the inherited table (position-based), so no regression there. Actually with the inherited table, `rate.?limit` would match the first line ending at "limit" (~column 26 of line 1), and "API Error" ends later, so UnknownApiError would also win. Same behavior.

But here's a subtle behavioral difference introduced by the anchored patterns: with `^` anchoring and `[^\r\n]*` spans, the anchored pattern's match now spans THE ENTIRE LINE from line start to line end. This extends match.end() to the end of the 429 line. With the old unanchored `rate.?limit`, match ended at "limit" (or "rate limit" end). Hmm, could the extended match end swallow a classification that previously won?

Scenario: a line containing BOTH "429 rate limit" text AND "Connection refused" AFTER it on the same line... e.g. `429 rate limit reached (connection refused?)`. With old pattern: `rate.?limit` ends at ~col 13; `Connection refused` ends at end of line → NetworkConnectionError wins (correct-ish). With new anchored pattern: rate-limit match ends at END of line (because `[^\r\n]*` trailing span) → position tie: both end at line end. `match.end() > last_match[0]` is strict greater-than, so FIRST-compiled wins on ties. Pattern compile order: rate-limit patterns are FIRST in the table (inherited order — after the override, rate-limit entries were originally first; the override filters ApiRateLimitError entries and appends the anchored pair AT THE END). On a tie (both matches end at the same position), the FIRST pattern in iteration order wins (`match.end() > last_match[0]` strict).
